task_title: Don't take inflated metrics at face value
output: {"concerns":["Growth Lead employer is unnamed (2023-2024), so company context, stage, and claim credibility cannot be assessed from the CV.","Growth Lead outcomes are stated without baselines, timeframe detail, or ownership scope: 'Increased revenue 300%. Managed a $5M budget. Grew the team 10x.'","Prior role evidence is narrow relative to a Growth Marketing Manager scope: Marketing Associate, Brightline (2021-2023) only notes 'ran email campaigns.'","Total dated marketing timeline is short and thinly evidenced (Associate 2021-2023; Growth Lead 2023-2024) with no channel/program detail beyond email plus listed skills.","Skills are self-listed (SEO, paid ads, 'data-driven growth') without CV examples tying them to campaigns, spend, or results."],"recommendation":"clarify","verify":["Confirm employer name, business model, stage, and Vance's exact title/scope for the 2023-2024 Growth Lead role.","Verify the 300% revenue increase: baseline revenue, period, Vance's direct ownership vs. team/company factors, and proof (dashboards, board decks, references).","Verify the $5M budget: what it covered (paid, lifecycle, brand, etc.), approval authority, and performance against targets.","Verify 'grew the team 10x': starting vs. ending headcount, hiring vs. matrixed reports, and Vance's management responsibilities.","Probe Brightline (2021-2023) email work: list size, lifecycle vs. promo, tools, metrics (open/click/revenue), and any broader growth duties.","Confirm hands-on depth in SEO and paid ads with concrete campaigns, spend levels, and measured outcomes—not skills-list only."]}
